Porlamar|Venezuela.f: In 1561 the rebel Lope de Aguirre came to Margarita, killed the acting governor, seized the treasury in Porlamar and burned its harbour.

Guanaja|Honduras.f: Columbus landed on Guanaja in 1502, named it Isla de los Pinos, and first came across cacao there.

Providencia|Colombia.f: English Puritans founded a colony on Providencia in 1629 through the Providence Island Company, and Spain took it in 1641.

Kaieteur Falls|Guyana.f: Kaieteur Falls on the Potaro River is 226 m high and ranks as the highest-flow single-drop waterfall in the world.

Caye Caulker|Belize.f: Hurricane Hattie in 1961 gets credit for Caye Caulker's Split, but villagers actually dredged it by hand after the storm opened a gap.

San Pedro|Belize.f: San Pedro was founded in 1848 by Mestizo refugees fleeing the Caste War in Yucatan.
